summary.short: EU regulation setting common rules for media services in the internal market. Requires Member States to safeguard editorial independence, journalistic sources and public service media; creates the European Board for Media Services; imposes ownership disclosure, state-advertising, audience-measurement and very-large-platform duties. Applies from 8 August 2025, some provisions earlier.
summary.long: Establishes a common framework for media services in the internal market to safeguard editorial independence and media pluralism. Chapter II sets recipient rights, editorial-freedom and journalistic-source protections (limiting surveillance and spyware, with narrow derogations), public service media safeguards, and ownership and state-advertising disclosure duties for media providers. Chapter III designates national regulatory authorities, creates the European Board for Media Services to replace ERGA, and sets cooperation procedures and coordination of measures against media services from outside the Union. Section 4 requires very large online platforms to offer media providers a self-declaration function (including on AI-generated content), give statements of reasons with a 24-hour reply, run a structured dialogue and let users customise device settings. Section 5 covers national measures and media market concentration assessments; Section 6 covers audience measurement transparency and allocation of state advertising funds. It requires monitoring and a 2028 evaluation and contains no penalty provisions. Application is staged from 8 November 2024 to 8 May 2027.

enforcement.note: The text contains no penalty, fine, criminal sanction, licence revocation, clawback, suspension-by-authority or blocking regime, and no article on Member State penalties. Article 4(3) prohibits Member States from certain measures and is not a sanction regime. Article 18(4) concerns a very large online platform's own decisions to suspend or restrict visibility of media content, not an enforcement sanction. Article 26 is a monitoring exercise, not an enforcement sanction.
